newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia's Ecopetrol leadership shakeup seen - paper.
newsitem.headline: Colombia's Ecopetrol leadership shakeup seen - paper.

text.p: Three board members of state oil company Ecopetrol have been replaced amid controversy involving the British Petroleum Co, Bogota's El Espectador newspaper said Tuesday.

The newspaper quoted veteran government board representative Jose Fernando Isaza Delgado as saying he had been forced to step down because of his opposition to BP's calls for more profitable concession terms in its Piedemonte exploration contract.

Under the contract's current sliding-scale formula, BP's and Ecopetrol divide profits equally for total production of less than 60 million barrels. The state share increases to a top rate of 70 percent when total production reaches 150 million barrels.
Piedemonte has estimated reserves of about one billion barrels of natural gas liquids and 10 trillion cubic feet of natural gas in the Pauto, Florena and Volcanera discoveries.
BP has argued that the sliding scale formula makes exploitation of Piedemonte economically unviable.
Ecopetrol has officially said that it was considering improving the concession terms.
But Isaza told El Espectador that any change in a signed contract would set a dangerous precedent.
The change would be sure to spark demands from other foreign oil companies operating in Colombia for more profitable contract terms, he said.
In addition to Isaza, who sat on Ecopetrol's board for the past 10 years, El Espectador said two other members had been replaced in a shakeup Monday night.
The other members were identified as Cesar Gonzalez, head of the National Banking Association, and Carlos Gonzalez Vargas.
Cesar Gonzalez told El Espetador that he too had opposed granting more favorable concession terms to BP.
Spokesmen for Ecopetrol could not be reached for immediate comment.
